caption: Finally into the summer research block - Anna's at Westbrook through Friday for their end-of-year thing and I've had the mornings completely uninterrupted. It's been productive.
Love that for you. Steve in town this week or traveling again?
Traveling, back Thursday. Which means I'm also doing school pickup, so the window isn't as clean as I'd like.
Lunch Thursday before his flight lands? I found that Moroccan place on Thornfield Ave is apparently decent.
Define decent. Last time you said that we ended up at a salad bar with ambient techno.
😂 I deserved that. Legitimately good this time. Tagine, proper mint tea, no detectable speakers.
Thursday works if we're done by 1:30. I have pickup at 3 and I refuse to rush through a tagine.
1pm, I'll book it. You deserve actual food after a week of solo parenting plus genomics.
Deep-focus morning wrapped by noon. Perahia's Bach on repeat. Kitchen herbs thriving.
Advanced class did the adage cleanly today. Sixteen years of teaching, still catches me.
Sunday cornbread with Anna - she measures with confidence I did not have at fourteen.
Voss revision three finally submitted. The methods section is 320 words lighter.
Thornfield after the storm. The maples are absurd this year.
First real frost - the herb garden retreats indoors.
Tenure dossier is in. Whatever the outcome, the work stands.
49 today. Quiet dinner, one candle, three phone calls.
Thanksgiving with the Boston contingent visiting. Anna organized the seating chart.
Christmas Eve, Fenway snow, mother's roast. As it should be.
Boxing Day walk with Dad. He is faster than he thinks.
New Year at home. No resolutions - just the next deadline.
Winter Symposium at MIT. Talks about symmetry breaking that will not leave my head.
Cambridge in January is beautiful in a way that only Cambridge in January is.
Annual physical done. TSH slightly high, adjusting dose. Back on the mat tomorrow.
Steve's birthday - homemade pasta, no candles, correct.
Anna is 15. It happened while I was reviewing a manuscript.
Barre work with the advanced students. They are ready for the March showcase.
Whitfield year-3 budget update in. On to closeout planning.
Anna's spring soccer opener. She scored twice; the coach is unsurprised.
Patricia's birthday - she still picks up first.
Whitfield closeout planning meeting. Three years, one grant, one hundred pages of a report.
March 31 - the grant closes. On to the next.
Snow melting on the front step. Rosemary is unfazed.
Ryan defended his job talk to the group. He is ready.
Sarah's manuscript is in review at Bioinformatics. Two years of work.
Wei passed his qualifying exam. The room applauded before he finished.
Boston again for Mom's birthday. Cake, tea, no fuss.
Anna's new soccer boots - the ballet shoes are on the shelf now.
Reading The Ashford editorial. Progress on the field is still slow but real.
Sunday piano - Gould's 1981 Goldberg is still the answer.
Ballet parents newsletter went out. Klaviyo is easier than I expected.
The Trader Joe's line has a personality this week.
Steve fixed the P-trap. Small victories.
Anna's homework interrupted by a text from her grandmother. Both won.
Yoga at 5:45 today. Extra ten minutes for the neck.
Karen dinner at the usual place. Two hours, no phones.
The Ashford Journal of Molecular Biology accepted the Voss paper. R3 was the last round.
Faculty holiday party. I made small talk for exactly seventy-five minutes.
Instagram is not my medium but occasionally the light in Thornfield insists.
